title: How many notes of each kind are in a big pile of money?
description: Meera's mother counts a month's money in her stationery shop in Pune. The video finds the notes of ten, one hundred, five hundred and the thousands in a five digit amount.
teaching_notes: One idea: cutting digits from the right counts tens, hundreds and thousands, and the same works for five digit numbers. Watch for the first digit being read as thousands.

source: Let Us Do (second set) 9 (e) to (h), notes in 65,342
video_script.why: The child has counted notes in a four digit amount, but not in a five digit one.
video_script.substitution: Cut the digits from the right to count each kind of note; take away the extra hundreds and divide by five for notes of five hundred.
video_script.anchor: Meera's mother counting the month's money in her stationery shop in Pune
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu reads the first digit of sixty five thousand as thousands. That digit sits in the ten thousands place, so the thousands are sixty five.
video_script.payoff_line: cut the digits from the right

final_answer.value: 6,534 notes of 10, 653 notes of 100, 65 thousands and 130 notes of 500
final_answer.spoken: one hundred and thirty notes of five hundred and sixty five thousands

maths_rules: 65,342 rupees: cut 1 digit leaves 6,534, so 6,534 notes of 10 with 2 left
cut 2 digits leaves 653, so 653 notes of 100 with 42 left
slip: the first digit 6 gives 6 thousands; the thousands are really 65
hint example: 1,250 gives 125 tens and 12 hundreds
video_script.design: Exercise. Hint: the same cutting of digits works at any size. A small cash box of 1,250 rupees shows it before the child tries again.

beats.on_screen: a photo of the pile of rupee notes sits behind as a dimmed backdrop and fades at the end of the beat; a small title card From your book; a stationery shop counter with a cash box marked 65,342 rupees; four empty boxes labelled notes of 10, notes of 100, thousands and notes of 500

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.story: a cash box with 65,342 rupees appears at the shop
marks.ask: four empty boxes appear: notes of 10, notes of 100, thousands, notes of 500

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='story'/>Meera's mother keeps a stationery shop in Pune. She counts the month's money, sixty five thousand three hundred and forty two rupees.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many notes of ten and of one hundred are in it? How many thousands, and how many notes of five hundred?

beats.on_screen: the items hold still and the anchor gets an accent underline

marks.stop: the anchor is underlined in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Stop the video. Say your answer out loud.

beats.on_screen: a small cash box of 1,250 rupees: cutting one digit gives 125 notes of 10, cutting two gives 12 notes of 100; a hint note appears

marks.ex: 1,250 rupees appears in a small box

narration: <bookmark mark='ex'/>Take one thousand two hundred and fifty rupees.
<bookmark mark='tens'/>Cutting one digit leaves one hundred and twenty five notes of ten.
<bookmark mark='hunds'/>Cutting two digits leaves twelve notes of one hundred.
<bookmark mark='hint'/>The same cutting works for any size of number. Try again with this.

beats.on_screen: Chintu's bubble shows 6 thousands from the first digit of 65,342; 6,000 appears beside 65,342; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.chintu: Chintu's bubble appears with the wrong count
marks.strike: the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>The first digit is six, so there are six thousands.
<bookmark mark='small'/>Six thousand rupees is far less than sixty five thousand three hundred and forty two.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>That first digit sits in the ten thousands place, and it is worth sixty thousand.

beats.on_screen: the rule line appears; 65,342 with one digit cut shows 6,534; with two cut shows 653; with three cut shows 65

marks.tens: 65,342 with the 2 cut shows 6,534 in the box notes of 10
marks.hunds: 65,342 with 42 cut shows 653 in the box notes of 100
marks.thou: 65,342 with 342 cut shows 65 in the box thousands

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Cut the digits from the right, and read what is left.
<bookmark mark='tens'/>Cutting one digit leaves six thousand five hundred and thirty four. That is the number of notes of ten.
<bookmark mark='hunds'/>Cutting two digits leaves six hundred and fifty three notes of one hundred.
<bookmark mark='thou'/>Cutting three digits leaves sixty five thousands.

beats.on_screen: 653 hundreds: 3 hundreds taken away leaves 650; 650 ÷ 5 = 130; the box notes of 500 shows 130
narration: <bookmark mark='away'/>Take away the three extra hundreds, and six hundred and fifty hundreds are left.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Five hundreds make one note, so we divide six hundred and fifty by five.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>That gives one hundred and thirty notes of five hundred.

beats.on_screen: a check: 130 × 500 = 65,000, and 65,342 − 65,000 = 342 is less than one more note of 500
narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>To check, multiply back. One hundred and thirty notes of five hundred make sixty five thousand rupees.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Three hundred and forty two rupees are left, less than one more note of five hundred.
